questions.q: What does table-level lineage record, according to this lesson?
options: Which tables feed which other tables, without specifying which columns are involved
Which specific columns feed which specific columns
The total storage size of every table in a database
The names of every user who has queried a table
questions.explain: Table-level lineage is coarse — it shows a relationship between two tables as a whole, like 'stg.Orders_Clean feeds dw.FactSales,' without column detail.

questions.q: In the CustomerNotes example, why does a table-level lineage arrow give a false sense of having answered an impact-analysis question?
options: Because the arrow implies every column in the source might matter to every column in the target, when a specific column might not be used downstream at all
Because table-level lineage is always factually incorrect
Because CustomerNotes is a column that cannot exist in any real system
Because table-level lineage only applies to tables with exactly 15 columns
questions.explain: The single table-to-table arrow doesn't say which columns the relationship actually covers, so it can't tell you whether a specific column change is safe — you'd have to dig into the code to find out.

questions.q: Which of these is given as a real cost of column-level lineage that explains why it isn't used everywhere?
options: It requires parsing actual transformation logic and produces a much larger volume of edges to maintain
It is illegal in most regulated industries
It can only be captured once per year
It eliminates the need for any table-level lineage at all
questions.explain: Column-level lineage is more expensive to capture (requires parsing real logic), larger in volume (many more edges), and more prone to going stale when transformation logic changes.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what connects the choice to reserve column-level lineage for specific columns to the prior Metadata Management course?
options: It mirrors the idea of critical data elements — fields important enough to justify the extra documentation cost
It mirrors the idea that all metadata should be deleted after one year
It has no connection to anything covered in the prior course
It mirrors the idea that only technical staff should ever see any lineage diagram
questions.explain: Just as critical data elements earn extra documentation rigor in the Metadata Management course, the highest-value columns earn the extra cost of column-level lineage here.

questions.q: According to the 'when to use which' guidance in this lesson, which situation calls for column-level lineage rather than table-level?
options: Checking whether it's safe to rename a specific column that feeds a critical report
Getting a quick overview of the overall shape of a pipeline architecture
Documenting hundreds of low-priority internal staging tables
Counting how many tables exist in a database
questions.explain: Column-level lineage is reserved for situations requiring precision, like confirming a specific column rename is safe — table-level is sufficient for broad architecture overviews or low-priority tables.
